questions.q: A pump returned for cleaning has an expired preventive maintenance label. What do you do?
options: Clean it and send it straight back to the nursing unit
Remove the label and reuse the pump
Pull it and send it to biomedical engineering
Store it with the clean equipment
questions.explain: Equipment without current preventive maintenance cannot be issued. It is tagged out and sent to biomedical engineering, which checks it and applies a new label before it returns to service.

questions.q: During inspection you see a frayed power cord on a patient care device. What is correct?
options: Tape the cord and dispatch the device
Tag it out of service and report it for repair
Send it to the unit with a warning note taped on it
Cut off the frayed part
questions.explain: Damaged cords are an electrical hazard. The device is removed from service, labeled as defective and sent to biomedical engineering; it is never repaired on the spot by sterile processing staff.

questions.q: What happens to single-use consumables attached to returned equipment?
options: They are removed and discarded before cleaning
They are cleaned and reused
They are sterilized with the device
They stay attached so the next patient can use them
questions.explain: Tubing, sleeves, pads and other disposable parts are taken off and discarded as waste before the device is cleaned, so every surface can be reached and nothing used goes to another patient.

questions.q: Where should clean, ready-to-use patient care equipment be kept?
options: In the decontamination room
In the hallway next to the soiled room, under a cover
In a closed vehicle outside
In a clean, dry, secure area, charged if needed
questions.explain: Clean equipment is stored apart from soiled equipment, protected from dust and moisture, and plugged in or with charged batteries so it works when a unit calls for it.

questions.q: Why is one-way flow kept in the patient care equipment area?
options: To speed up battery charging for every returned device
Because devices only fit one way
To keep soiled equipment apart from clean equipment
To shorten inventory counts
questions.explain: Soiled devices arrive at one end and leave clean and labeled at the other. Keeping the flow in one direction stops clean equipment from being contaminated by returns.

questions.q: What does an equipment tracking system, manual, computer or RFID, make possible?
options: Sterilizing devices automatically
Knowing where each device is and its status
Charging staff for lost equipment
Replacing the manufacturer's instructions for each device
questions.explain: Tracking shows which devices are in use, being cleaned, ready or out for repair, including rentals and loaners. It speeds up deliveries and supports maintenance schedules and recalls.
